text:
mira: Seeing elevated queue lengths on eu-west2 GPU pool, dropping steady-state capacity by ~30%. Alerts show 'allocation-failed: insufficient capacity'.

sam: Thanks Mira. Which pool? fabric-gpu-prod or batch-gpu?

mira: fabric-gpu-prod. Looks correlated with a rolling preempt event from the cloud provider around 04:12 UTC. Eviction spikes and then kube-scheduler thrash.

jonah: infra-bot just posted an incident: `INC-2026-0421-euw2-capacity` — severity=P2.

infra-bot: automatic: high_eviction_rate detected in cluster eu-west2-fabric. Notifying oncall rotation. Suggested mitigation: scale fallback-pool, route low-priority traffic to dedicated-readonly.

alex: Oncall, I'm on it. Reallocating canary traffic now. Mira, can you run `kubectl get nodes -l pool=fabric-gpu-prod -o wide` and paste results?

mira: Pasting output snippet: ```
NAME                         STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-prod-12                  Ready    <none>   42d   v1.28.3
gpu-prod-13                  Ready    <none>   14d   v1.28.3
gpu-prod-14                  NotReady <none>   2h    v1.28.3
```

mira: Node gpu-prod-14 shows kernel oom_killer messages in dmesg, then became NotReady.

sam: OK. Short-term plan: 1) Drain and cordon gpu-prod-14. 2) Spin up fallback nodes in eu-west2-dedicated (spot->on-demand fallback). 3) Adjust routing weight to avoid fabric-gpu-prod until stable.

alex: I'll handle cordon/drain: `kubectl cordon gpu-prod-14 && kubectl drain gpu-prod-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

jonah: While Alex drains, we should tweak the paging policy: current policy escalates to rotation for ANY cluster eviction alert. That wakes the whole rotation for transient spot evictions. Propose change: only page for sustained eviction_rate > 10m window OR if capacity_remains < 70%.

mira: +1. This would reduce noise when provider-side preemptions spike for short windows. Also add an automated mitigation step in infra-bot: if fallback capacity available, infra-bot should suppress paging and post a status update instead.

sam: Agree. We need small policy tweak: in pagerflow config, change `eviction_window_seconds` from 60 to 600 and add `min_capacity_threshold_pct: 70`. Example patch snippet: ```yaml
- trigger: eviction_rate
- params:
    window_seconds: 60
+    window_seconds: 600
+    min_capacity_threshold_pct: 70
```

jonah: Make sure this goes through a short review; we don't want to hide real outages. Add an override flag `force_page: true` for SRE to bypass suppression.

alex: Draining done. Moving batch of pods to fallback-pool. Traffic weights rerouted: fabric-gpu-prod -> 0.55, fallback-pool -> 0.45. Observing latency 95p increase ~120ms for some endpoints.

mira: Noted. Will monitor request failures. If error rate climbs >1%, we'll do a partial rollback of routing.

infra-bot: status: fallback capacity healthy (12/12 nodes), evictions decreased, monitoring window shows eviction_rate trending down. Paging suppressed per new temporary rule (automation).

sam: Next actions: 1) Create a short RFC for permanent pagerflow policy change, include metrics from this incident. 2) Add a runbook step to ensure oncall rotation gets an explicit notify when infra-bot suppresses paging. 3) Schedule a handoff doc update for next rotation.

jonah: I'll draft the RFC and post to eng-oncall/eng-infra channels. Alex — can you run `kubectl uncordon` on healthy replacements after pods settle?

alex: Will do in 15m.

mira: Thanks team. Good run — mitigation succeeded. We'll reconvene if error rate or evictions spike again. :white_check_mark:
